name: Developer widget
summary: A widget of tabs over live monitors for development: the pipeline chart, the scheduled chart and a sent list of your Task Manager sends and a log tab of the server log, each updating live.
description: The developer widget is a tab strip over a list of monitors. The pipeline tab is the pipeline widget itself: the plugin status squares with the engine's status line (no rebuild button there; rebuild from Settings, pipeline), what is running now and the queue, and the pipeline chart of recent runs (name, area, run time, how long ago, runs); the pipeline tab came back 2026-10-12 on the owner's request, #1689, after the other operator's #1682 U1 removed the old job version. The scheduled tab is a chart in the same look (item 542, #1701): one row per automation with its name, what ran its last run in plain words (schedule, missed run, retry, run now by the owner's name, or run now by an agent's session name), its area (the session it messages, else its project, else machine), how long the last run took, how long ago, and the next run. Over the chart two short sections (2026-10-12): running lists each automation run in progress with what ran it and how long it has run, and queue lists the next scheduled fires soonest first (automations' next runs and, with the task manager plugin on, scheduled task items), at most eight and then "+N more"; both follow the global / sessions / both switch. The figure columns keep the room their widest value needs, so a run time is never cut off. A narrow tab drops the area and then what ran it, never the run time, and a next run a day or more away reads in days and hours (in 6d 23h), so a weekly or monthly schedule is never cut off either. The mark before a name is a shape as well as a color: a filled circle ok, a diamond error, a dash skipped. A global / sessions / both switch on top picks Carnivore's automations (global), the task manager's scheduled task items with their next fire (sessions, read only while the task manager plugin is on; with it off the sessions view says so), or both; the choice is remembered in this browser. Who pressed run now is kept in the run's own notes when the button is pressed (no new column). The scheduled tab updates from the server's pushes (the automations and automation runs topics, and the task manager's list topic), and the pipeline tab from the pipeline topic, with no timed polling while the live connection is up; only the selected tab reads anything, and the chosen tab is remembered in this browser. The selected tab is the lighter fill and the other tabs the darker one. A new monitor is one entry in the widget's monitor list. The sent tab (the owner, 2026-10-14, #1805: "a small flowing list like the others in the dev widget so i can monitor when i send things") is the pipeline tab's layout: a strip on top with a status line ("3 in this browser, 1 not sent") and the copy all and download keys, then "in this browser" (the copies the browser outbox still holds because the server did not answer or refused them, each with retry, copy and, on a refused one, discard keys), then the chart of your recent Task Manager replies, answers, board rounds and adds with where each stands with the agent: waiting to tell, telling in a few seconds, holding while the agent is busy, told with the agent's name and when, read, filed, or not told and why. It updates from the server's pushes with no polling at idle, and with the Task Manager plugin off it still shows the copies kept in this browser. The log tab (the owner, 2026-10-15, #1827: "a log viewer to the dev widget as a new tab, top strip is buttons for each status to filter each type. scrolling not all inclusive") is, since #1861, the one shared log viewer, the same one the logs page (#logs, and the menu bar's Logs... row) shows. It reads records, not lines: a Python traceback or stderr text stays with the event it follows, its line count shows on the row in the danger color and opening the row shows the whole record as JSON with the traceback under it. A strip on top has one toggle for each level (error, warn, info, debug), all on at first and remembered in this browser, one chip per source, the server's log level (changed live, or back to the .env value), export (the records shown, as a .jsonl download) and clear. Under it a text filter (write /pattern/ for a regular expression) and a session filter that matches any of the ways the log names a session. Click a field on a row to show only that value, Alt-click to hide it; each active field filter is a chip you click to remove. The list follows new records at the bottom; scrolling up pauses it and a "N new, jump to live" button brings it back. Load older pages back through the file and its rotated copies. The viewer keeps at most 10,000 records or 8 MB and says when it drops the oldest. Secrets are masked again before anything is shown. It updates from the server's pushes with no polling at idle.
where: Home screen once added: a cell titled developer with a tab strip (pipeline, scheduled, sent, log).
The drawer widget area, once added.
The scheduled tab's top strip holds the global, sessions, both switch.
The sent tab's top strip holds the copy all and download keys.
The log tab's top strip holds one toggle per level: error, warn, info, debug.
how_to: Open the edit layout control at the bottom of the drawer.
Search widgets for developer; press the card to put it on the home page or in the drawer.
Press the scheduled tab to see the scheduled chart; press global, sessions or both to choose what it lists.
Press pipeline to go back to the pipeline chart.
Press the sent tab to see what you sent and whether the agent was told.
If a send shows under in this browser, press retry to send it now, copy to take its text, or discard to drop a refused one; copy all and download take everything.
Press the log tab to read the newest server log lines; press a level to hide or show its lines, your choice is remembered.
Scroll up to read older lines; scroll back to the bottom and the list follows new lines again.
examples: Press run now on an automation and see run now by your name in the ran by column.
Switch to sessions to see the task manager's scheduled task items and when each fires next.
Spot a failed scheduled run at a glance from its error mark.
See which automation is running right now and what fires next, under the global, sessions or both choice.
Reply on a task while the server restarts and see the reply sit in this browser, then land on its own with the agent told.
Download the outbox as a file after a long outage to keep every word you typed.
Raise the server log level to debug in settings, then watch the debug lines appear in the log tab.
Press everything off but error to see only the last errors.
